newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-ECCENTRIC PARNEVIK IN CONTENTION AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ECCENTRIC PARNEVIK IN CONTENTION AGAIN.

text.p: Jesper Parnevik wears a cap with an upturned brim, eats volcanic dust to clear mercury from his intestines and reportedly likes "fast-vibrating" food.
It is hard to escape the conclusion that if golf did not intervene, Parnevik could happily devote himself full-time to being an eccentric.

His golf, however, is far from offbeat and on Friday the colourful son of Sweden's most famous comedian and impersonator fired himself into contention for the British Open title with a five-under-par 66.

Nothing outlandish there and certainly no need for the large flashing glasses which he has been known to don while travelling by plane and which he says help synchronise the left and right sides of the brain.

Besides the volcanic dust, obtained from health food stores, Parnevik eats a lot of fruit because a dietician told him the action of the earth in spinning creates very fast vibrations and most bodies move too slowly to keep up.
Fruit is apparently a "fast-vibrating" food that helps the body keep up with the pace.
Something is clearly working.
Parnevik finished second in the 1994 British Open at Turnberry and on Friday he played himself into position to go one better at Royal Troon this weekend.
The close defeat by Nick Price three years ago has not left any scars on Parnevik, even though it was his for the taking until he bogeyed the final hole after thinking he needed a birdie.
He had neglected to look at the leaderboard and lost by one stroke.
"At that very moment, of course I was a little bit crushed about it," he said.
"But looking back a few hours afterwards, it was as much fun as I've had playing any golf tournament.
"It was my first time ever up there in a major and I couldn't expect to be that lucky to win the very first time.
"Looking back, I have nothing but positive thought about it. I learned a lot and it gave me a great confidence boost."

The Swede, now based on the U.S. Tour where he has had seven top-five finishes this year, began his surge in Thursday's first round when he birdied the last three holes for a 70, the last two on putts of 20 and 25 feet.
Then he decided to change putters. "It didn't feel right yesterday. My game and my putting felt terrible all day," he said.

On Friday, he set off by three-putting the first green for a bogey. But an eagle three after a three-iron to six feet at the fourth got him going and after four birdies he closed out with a 50-foot putt to save par at the last.
Parnevik, who first announced his intention to win the British Open when he was 13, called his finish "an unbelievable par".
"Those are the things that happen in this tournament -- a tournament that almost makes your hair stand on end when you play it," he said.
He does not know if he can go on and win on Sunday.
"It all depends if I can get the right breaks. My game doesn't feel as good as the scores are. I am playing on momentum and playing well."
He said his game felt best last week at the Loch Lomond World Invitational, "but I didn't score very well". He finished joint 16th.
As for his unorthodox habits, he first turned up the brim of his cap five years ago to improve his sun tan "because I was very pale from the Swedish winter".
He has said that the mercury in his body comes from eating fish and he has also had the fillings in his teeth replaced with ceramic ones.
The brain-synchronising glasses, he has also said, "are to balance the neutral firings in my brain".
